Report Customization

This guide shows how to generate customized reports from power flow solutions with control over units, formatting, and column selection.

The Basic Workflow

using Powerful
using PowerFlowData
using DataFrames

# Solve power flow
case = parse_network("cases/ieee14.raw")
sys = SystemModel(case)
prob = ACPowerFlowProblem(sys)
sol = solve(prob, NewtonRaphson())

# Generate report (default configuration)
bus_data = collect_model_table(sol, :Bus)
df = DataFrame(bus_data)

This gives you a table with:

  • Physical power units (MW/MVAR)
  • Per-unit voltages
  • Angles in degrees
  • Descriptive column names with units

Let's explore how to customize this.

Understanding Report Configuration

Reports are controlled by ReportConfig, which has three main components:

config = ReportConfig(
    units = UnitPreferences(power=:physical, voltage=:pu),
    formatting = FormattingPreferences(float_precision=4),
    columns = ColumnPreferences(include_id=true, use_descriptions=true)
)

1. Unit Preferences

Control what units appear in the output:

UnitPreferences(
    power = :physical,      # :physical (MW/MVAR) or :pu
    voltage = :pu,          # :pu or :kv
    angle = :deg,           # :deg or :rad
    impedance = :pu,        # :pu or :ohm
    base_mva = 100.0        # System base power
)

Examples:

# All physical units (MW, kV, degrees)
config = ReportConfig(units=UnitPreferences(
    power = :physical,
    voltage = :kv,
    angle = :deg
))
bus_data = collect_model_table(sol, :Bus, config=config)

# All per-unit (engineering analysis)
config = ReportConfig(units=UnitPreferences(
    power = :pu,
    voltage = :pu,
    angle = :rad
))
bus_data = collect_model_table(sol, :Bus, config=config)

2. Formatting Preferences

Control how values are displayed:

FormattingPreferences(
    float_precision = 4     # Decimal places (used by print_model_table)
)

Note: Formatting only affects print_model_table(). Use collect_model_table() for full precision data export.

3. Column Preferences

Control which columns appear and how they're named:

ColumnPreferences(
    use_descriptions = true,              # Use descriptive names vs field names
    include_units = true,                 # Append "(MW)", "(pu)" to names
    column_style = :short,                # :compact, :short, :verbose
    include_id = true,                    # Include instance ID column
    include_vars = nothing,               # Vector{Symbol} to select specific vars
    exclude_vars = Symbol[],              # Exclude these variables
    include_params = true,                # Include model parameters
    exclude_params = Symbol[]             # Exclude these parameters
)

Column Style Options:

# :compact - Just variable names, no units
config = ReportConfig(columns=ColumnPreferences(column_style=:compact))
# → "P_from", "Q_from", "V", "Theta"

# :short - Variable names with units (default)
config = ReportConfig(columns=ColumnPreferences(column_style=:short))
# → "P_from (MW)", "Q_from (MVAR)", "V (pu)", "Theta (deg)"

# :verbose - Full descriptions
config = ReportConfig(columns=ColumnPreferences(column_style=:verbose))
# → "Active power from-side (MW)", "Reactive power from-side (MVAR)"

Preset Configurations

Five presets are available for common use cases:

Default

MW power, per-unit voltage, degrees (excludes initial values):

bus_data = collect_model_table(sol, :Bus)  # Uses Default preset
# or explicitly:
bus_data = collect_model_table(sol, :Bus, config=Default)

AllPerUnit

Everything in per-unit (useful for engineering analysis):

bus_data = collect_model_table(sol, :Bus, config=AllPerUnit)

AllPhysical

Everything in physical units (MW, kV, degrees):

bus_data = collect_model_table(sol, :Bus, config=AllPhysical)

Minimal

Variables only, no parameters, compact names:

bus_data = collect_model_table(sol, :Bus, config=Minimal)

Compact

Fewer decimal places for quick inspection:

print_model_table(sol, :Bus, config=Compact)

Selecting Variables

Include Only Specific Variables

# Only voltage and angle
config = ReportConfig(columns=ColumnPreferences(
    include_vars = [:v, :theta]
))
bus_data = collect_model_table(sol, :Bus, config=config)

# Only branch power flows (exclude losses)
config = ReportConfig(columns=ColumnPreferences(
    include_vars = [:p_from, :q_from, :p_to, :q_to]
))
branch_data = collect_model_table(sol, :Branch, config=config)

Exclude Specific Variables

# All bus variables except angle
config = ReportConfig(columns=ColumnPreferences(
    exclude_vars = [:theta]
))
bus_data = collect_model_table(sol, :Bus, config=config)

Discovering Available Variables

Use the discovery API to see what's available:

# All possible outputs (DAE variables + observations)
available = get_available_outputs(Bus)
# → [:v, :theta]

available = get_available_outputs(Branch)
# → [:p_from, :q_from, :p_to, :q_to, :p_loss, :q_loss]

# Default outputs (shown without explicit include_vars)
defaults = get_default_outputs(Branch)
# → [:p_from, :q_from, :p_to, :q_to]  # Losses excluded by default

Use in configuration:

# Include everything available (including non-defaults)
all_vars = get_available_outputs(Branch)
config = ReportConfig(columns=ColumnPreferences(include_vars=all_vars))
branch_data = collect_model_table(sol, :Branch, config=config)
# Now includes p_loss and q_loss

Working with Parameters

By default, reports include both computed variables and model parameters (like base voltage, impedances).

Exclude All Parameters

config = ReportConfig(columns=ColumnPreferences(include_params=false))
bus_data = collect_model_table(sol, :Bus, config=config)
# Only solution variables (v, theta), no basekv, ide, etc.

Exclude Specific Parameters

# Exclude initial values (vm, va) from bus report
config = ReportConfig(columns=ColumnPreferences(
    exclude_params = [:vm, :va]
))
bus_data = collect_model_table(sol, :Bus, config=config)
# Shows computed solution but not initial guesses

Note: The Default preset already excludes [:vm, :va] to focus on solution values.

Exporting Reports

To DataFrame

using DataFrames

bus_data = collect_model_table(sol, :Bus)
df = DataFrame(bus_data)

# Now use DataFrame operations
filter(row -> row.V_pu > 1.05, df)  # High voltage buses
sort(df, :V_pu)                     # Sort by voltage

To CSV

using CSV

bus_data = collect_model_table(sol, :Bus, config=AllPhysical)
CSV.write("bus_results.csv", bus_data)

branch_data = collect_model_table(sol, :Branch)
CSV.write("branch_flows.csv", branch_data)

To Terminal (Pretty Print)

# Print to terminal with formatting
print_model_table(sol, :Bus)

# Custom formatting
config = ReportConfig(
    units = UnitPreferences(voltage=:kv),
    formatting = FormattingPreferences(float_precision=2)
)
print_model_table(sol, :Bus, config=config)

Multi-Island Systems

Reports automatically merge data from all islands:

# System with multiple islands
prob = ACPowerFlowProblem(sys)  # Auto-detects islands
sol = solve(prob, NewtonRaphson())

# Report includes all islands
bus_data = collect_model_table(sol, :Bus)
df = DataFrame(bus_data)

# All buses from all islands are in the table
# External IDs preserved (no confusion between islands)

Common Patterns

Generate Multiple Reports

# Physical units for presentation
bus_physical = collect_model_table(sol, :Bus, config=AllPhysical)
CSV.write("bus_results_physical.csv", bus_physical)

# Per-unit for analysis
bus_pu = collect_model_table(sol, :Bus, config=AllPerUnit)
CSV.write("bus_results_pu.csv", bus_pu)

Custom Report with Mixed Units

# MW power but kV voltage
config = ReportConfig(
    units = UnitPreferences(
        power = :physical,  # MW/MVAR
        voltage = :kv       # kV (not pu)
    ),
    columns = ColumnPreferences(
        exclude_params = [:vm, :va, :ide, :area, :zone, :owner]
    )
)
bus_data = collect_model_table(sol, :Bus, config=config)

Focused Analysis Report

# Only power flows, high precision
config = ReportConfig(
    units = UnitPreferences(power=:physical),
    formatting = FormattingPreferences(float_precision=6),
    columns = ColumnPreferences(
        include_vars = [:p_from, :q_from, :p_to, :q_to, :p_loss, :q_loss],
        include_params = false  # No impedances, ratings, etc.
    )
)
branch_data = collect_model_table(sol, :Branch, config=config)
df = DataFrame(branch_data)

# Find branches with high losses
high_loss = filter(row -> row.P_loss_MW > 1.0, df)

Compact Terminal Output

# Quick inspection during development
config = ReportConfig(
    formatting = FormattingPreferences(float_precision=2),
    columns = ColumnPreferences(
        include_vars = [:v, :theta],
        include_params = false,
        column_style = :compact
    )
)
print_model_table(sol, :Bus, config=config)

Understanding Unit Conversion

How It Works

Reports use two different conversion mechanisms:

1. Parameters (stored coefficients):

# During system setup, coefficients are saved
sys.pu_coeffs[:Bus][:basekv] = [1.0, 1.0, ...]  # Identity (kV → kV)

# Reports use exact inverse
physical = pu_value / coefficient

2. Observations (PUType-based):

# Computed values (like power flows) use PUType metadata
ActivePower()     → MW = pu * base_mva  (if power=:physical)
VoltageNominal() → kV = pu * base_kv    (if voltage=:kv)
AngleDegrees()   → deg = rad * 180/π    (if angle=:deg)

Base Quantities

Some conversions need base quantities (stored in model data):

# Voltage magnitude needs base_kv for kV conversion
config = ReportConfig(units=UnitPreferences(voltage=:kv))
bus_data = collect_model_table(sol, :Bus, config=config)
# Uses Bus.basekv for each bus

# Branch parameters use from-bus base voltage
branch_data = collect_model_table(sol, :Branch, config=config)
# Uses foreign reference: Branch.i → Bus.basekv

Under the hood (trait system):

# System uses traits to find base quantities (no hardcoded fields)
base_kv_vec = get_base_quantity_vector(sys, :Bus, BaseVoltage)

Validation and Error Messages

The report system validates your configuration upfront:

Invalid Variable Names

config = ReportConfig(columns=ColumnPreferences(
    include_vars = [:v, :theta, :nonexistent_var]
))
bus_data = collect_model_table(sol, :Bus, config=config)
# ERROR: Invalid variables in include_vars for :Bus: [:nonexistent_var].
#        Available: [:v, :theta]

Wrong Model for Variables

# Branch variables don't exist on Bus model
config = ReportConfig(columns=ColumnPreferences(
    include_vars = [:p_from, :q_from]  # These are Branch variables
))
bus_data = collect_model_table(sol, :Bus, config=config)
# ERROR: Invalid variables in include_vars for :Bus: [:p_from, :q_from].
#        Available: [:v, :theta]

Always check available variables first:

get_available_outputs(Bus)     # See what's available
get_default_outputs(Bus)       # See what's shown by default

Model-Specific Reports

Bus Results

bus_data = collect_model_table(sol, :Bus)
# Variables: :v (voltage magnitude), :theta (voltage angle)
# Parameters: :basekv, :ide (bus type), :area, :zone, :owner, :vm, :va

Branch Results

branch_data = collect_model_table(sol, :Branch)
# Default variables: :p_from, :q_from, :p_to, :q_to
# Available but not default: :p_loss, :q_loss
# Parameters: :r, :x, :b, :rate1, :rate2, :rate3, :status, etc.

# Include losses
config = ReportConfig(columns=ColumnPreferences(
    include_vars = [:p_from, :q_from, :p_to, :q_to, :p_loss, :q_loss]
))
branch_data = collect_model_table(sol, :Branch, config=config)

Generator Results

# PV generators
pv_data = collect_model_table(sol, :PV)
# Variables: depends on formulation
# Parameters: :pg, :qmax, :qmin, :vs (voltage setpoint), etc.

Advanced: Programmatic Configuration

Build configurations dynamically:

# Start with preset, modify parts
config = ReportConfig(
    AllPhysical,  # Base configuration
    columns = ColumnPreferences(  # Override columns
        exclude_params = [:vm, :va, :ide]
    )
)

# Or use keyword updates
base = AllPerUnit
custom = ReportConfig(
    base,
    formatting = FormattingPreferences(float_precision=6)
)

Performance Notes

collectmodeltable() vs printmodeltable()

# collect_model_table - Full precision, for export
data = collect_model_table(sol, :Bus)
CSV.write("data.csv", data)  # No rounding

# print_model_table - Applies formatting, for display
print_model_table(sol, :Bus, config=Compact)  # Rounded to 2 decimals

Repeated Reports

# If generating many reports, collect once then convert
bus_data = collect_model_table(sol, :Bus)

# Now use DataFrame operations (fast)
df = DataFrame(bus_data)
high_v = filter(row -> row.V_pu > 1.05, df)
low_v = filter(row -> row.V_pu < 0.95, df)

Key Insights

Same solution, multiple views: The power flow solution is in per-unit internally, but reports let you view it in any units you need.

Configuration is declarative: Specify what you want (units, columns, formatting), not how to compute it. The system handles unit conversions automatically.

Type-safe validation: Invalid variable names are caught immediately with helpful error messages listing available options.

The reporting system separates computation (solving power flow) from presentation (generating reports), letting you focus on analysis rather than data wrangling.
